name: Dr Uchenna Jerome Orji
summary: Researches and advises on regional and national policy and legal frameworks for ICT governance in Africa, including cybersecurity, telecommunications, data protection and artificial intelligence.
bio: Dr Uchenna Jerome Orji has extensive experience [researching](https://ng.linkedin.com/in/uchenna-jerome-orji-llm-phd-77063675) and [advising on regional and national policy and legal frameworks](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=uF7VIf8AAAAJ&hl=en) for the governance of information communications technologies in Africa, including cybersecurity, telecommunications, data protection and artificial intelligence. He is the author of [*Cybersecurity Law and Regulation* (Wolf Legal Publishers)](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/320624755_Cybersecurity_Law_and_Regulation), [*International Telecommunications Law and Policy* (Cambridge Scholars Publishing)](https://www.cambridgescholars.com/product/978-1-5275-0836-1), and [*Telecommunications Law and Regulation in Nigeria* (Cambridge Scholars Publishing)](https://www.cambridgescholars.com/product/978-1-5275-0675-6), in addition to several peer-reviewed papers analyzing frameworks governing ICT, cybersecurity, data protection and artificial intelligence in Africa. His articles have appeared in [*International Cybersecurity Law Review*](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1365/s43439-023-00109-7), [*Baltic Yearbook of International Law*](https://brill.com/view/journals/byio/20/1/article-p236_12.xml), [*Computer Law & Security Review*](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0267364919300159), *Computer and Telecommunications Law Review*, [*International Data Privacy Law*](https://academic.oup.com/idpl/article-abstract/7/3/179/4211051?redirectedFrom=fulltext), [*Tilburg Law Review*](https://tilburglawreview.com/articles/10.5334/tilr.137), [*Max Planck Institute for Comparative Public Law & International Law Research Paper Series*](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3930007), [*Masaryk University Journal of Law and Technology*](https://journals.muni.cz/mujlt/article/view/8666/9255), [*International Journal of Criminal Justice*](https://www.kicj.re.kr/board.es?mid=a20205010400&bid=0034&tag=&act=view&list_no=12210) and the [European Union Publications Office](https://op.europa.eu/en/publication-detail/-/publication/b8743238-489e-11ef-acbc-01aa75ed71a1/language-en).

Uchenna is a Fellow of the [African Center for Cyber Law and Cybercrime Prevention (ACCP)](https://cybercrime-fr.org/accp/) at the United Nations African Institute for the Prevention of Crime in Kampala, Uganda, and a Fellow of European School on Internet Governance, Germany. He was a Fellow of the [Global Scholars Academy](https://iglp.law.harvard.edu/events/2025gsa/) at the Institute for Global Law and Policy, Harvard Law School in 2025.

He has worked as a regional legal expert for a number of international and national organizations, including the [Commonwealth](https://thecommonwealth.org/news/commonwealth-report-calls-clearer-legislation-virtual-currencies), the [Council of Europe](https://www.coe.int/en/web/cybercrime/news/-/asset_publisher/S73WWxscOuZ5/content/cyber-legislation-in-the-ecowas-region), the [NATO Cooperative Cyber Defence Center of Excellence](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/natoccdcoe_baltic-yearbook-of-international-law-online-activity-7031529203825061888-jOZT/), the [Dutch Government](https://ict4peace.org/activities/ict4peace-a-comprehensive-normative-approach-to-cybersecurity-is-needed/), the Government of Nigeria’s [Presidential Advisory Committee Against Corruption](https://thenationonlineng.net/sagay-others-seek-regulatory-framework-virtual-currency/), and World Bank-funded projects for the harmonization of regional frameworks for digital governance in Africa. He has also been a speaker at several high-level international conferences on the governance of cybersecurity and artificial intelligence, and they include The Hague Conference on International Cybersecurity, the [European Union-CyberDirect](https://eucyberdirect.eu/events/closing-the-gap-2022) [Closing the Gap Conference](https://eucyberdirect.eu/events/closing-the-gap-2023), the [Global Cyber Policy Dialogues](https://static1.squarespace.com/static/5ca0ec9b809d8e4c67c27b3a/t/641df4b86765290ad4984c03/1679684793205/Southern+Africa+Cyber+Policy+Dialogue_Agenda+2022.pdf), [The Hague Global Conference on Cyber Space](https://ict4peace.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/05/16496284.pdf), [the NATO CCD COE’s International Conference on Cyber Conflict](https://ccdcoe.org/uploads/2018/10/Art-08-Multilateral-Legal-Responses-to-Cyber-Security-in-Africa-Any-Hope-for-Effective-International-Cooperation.pdf), the [Asian Security Conference](https://idsa.in/idsa-event/18th-asian-security-conference-securing-cyberspace-asian-and-international-perspectives-2), and [Global Conference on Cyber Capacity](https://www.worldbank.org/en/events/2024/01/04/global-conference-on-cyber-capacity-building-gc3b) (GC3B).

Uchenna is a Law Professor and was the [Chair of the Department of Commercial Law at the American University of Nigeria](https://www.aun.edu.ng/index.php/uchenna-jerome-orji) between 2020 and 2023. The Council for the Development of Social Science Research in Africa (CODESRIA) appointed him as the resource person/professor of cybersecurity policy for its 2016 [African Cybersecurity Governance Institute in Dakar](https://codesria.org/codesria-2016-democratic-governance-institute-the-african-state-and-public-cyber-security-service/), Senegal. He is a member of the Editorial Board of [*The Commonwealth Cybercrime Journal*](https://commonwealthconsultant.com/cyber-journal.html) published by the Commonwealth Secretariat, London and acts as External Examiner for doctoral theses at several universities.

Uchenna is an Attorney admitted to the Nigerian Bar. He holds an LL.M from the University of Ibadan, with specialization in cybersecurity law, and a PhD in Law from Nnamdi Azikiwe University, Nigeria, with specialization in telecommunications law. He is a Partner with [TETRALEX Legal & Advisory, Lagos, Nigeria](https://tetralex.com/dt_team/uchenna-j-orji/), and a Senior Fellow and Lead Researcher at AICTiG.

name: Dr Oghomwen Rita Ohiro
summary: Senior Lecturer in Public Law at the University of Benin and an expert in data protection and artificial intelligence law.
bio: Dr. Oghomwen Rita Ohiro is a Senior Lecturer in the Department of Public Law, Faculty of Law, University of Benin, Benin City, Nigeria. She is an expert in data protection and artificial intelligence law, with a research agenda focused on how African states can regulate data and AI in ways that protect fundamental rights while supporting innovation and development.

**Data protection and privacy:** Her work examines the legal frameworks governing personal data in Nigeria and beyond, including health data, consumer data, biometric identification, workplace monitoring, financial data and data protection in emergencies. She also writes on surveillance and the tension between national security and privacy.

**Artificial intelligence law:** She researches AI governance, AI and national security, deepfakes and reputational harm, facial recognition technology, and digital colonialism and data sovereignty in the Global South.
Her scholarship is comparative, drawing on India, the United Kingdom, the EU, Bangladesh and Tanzania. She brings academic depth and policy insight to the work of AICTiG.
expertise: Data sovereignty in the Global South
